def challenge[F[_], A](
      realm: String,
      store: AuthStore[F, A],
      blocker: Blocker,
      nonceCleanupInterval: Duration = 1.hour,
      nonceStaleTime: Duration = 1.hour,
      nonceBits: Int = 160,
  )(implicit
      F: Concurrent[F],
      t: Timer[F],
      cs: ContextShift[F],
  ): F[Kleisli[F, Request[F], Either[Challenge, AuthedRequest[F, A]]]] =
    NonceKeeperF[F](nonceStaleTime, nonceCleanupInterval, nonceBits, blocker)
      .map { nonceKeeper =>

      }

Source observation: gen accepts a Blocker but calls getRandomData directly under F.delay. Passing an argument alone is not proof of blocking isolation; reviews mention later helper integration.

evidence.excerpt:
test("DigestAuthentication should avoid many concurrent replay attacks") {
      val n = 100
      val results = for {
        digestAuthMiddleware <- DigestAuth.applyF(realm, plainTextAuthStore, testBlocker)
        digestAuthService = digestAuthMiddleware(service)
        challenge <- doDigestAuth1(digestAuthService.orNotFound)
        results <- (1 to n)
          .map(_ =>
            doDigestAuth2(digestAuthService.orNotFound, challenge, withReplay = false)
              .map(_._1.status)
          )
          .toList
          .parSequence
      } yield results

      results.map { res =>
        assertEquals(res.count(s => s == Ok), 1)
        assertEquals(res.count(s => s == Unauthorized), n - 1)
      }
evidence.interpretation: Source observation: concurrent replay test requires one successful request and remaining unauthorized responses. It exercises repeated use of the first counter, not arbitrary monotonically increasing counters.
Source observation: interval arithmetic uses monotonic nanoseconds and rejects a nonpositive refill period inside F. A val holding an effect is distinct from executing and memoizing its clock result.
Source observation: TestControl executes a program checking unavailable before refill and available after. This tests token state, not just elapsed sleep.

claims.rule: For stateful middleware and client factories, suspend allocation at the acquisition boundary and share that one acquired state across its requests; do not fix eagerness by recreating state per request.
claims.applicability: Historical pre-1.0 Cats Effect client allocation and CE2 DigestAuth show the same scope error in different APIs. This is a derived cross-case rule; use the target version's F/Resource constructors and retain the repository effect model.
claims.counterexample: Immutable configuration values with no owned executor, pool or mutable authentication state need not be delayed. An intentionally request-local counter is not middleware-wide state.

claims.rule: When making a published http4s middleware factory effectful on a compatibility-preserving branch, keep the promised legacy signature and compile concrete IO calls with defaults; use a distinct factory name when constraint-only overloads remain ambiguous.
claims.applicability: A narrow factory-specific procedure derived from the superseded #6077 and implemented #6138 discussion, not a new general MiMa or API-design checklist. Establish constraints from the actual new state implementation.
claims.counterexample: A deliberate incompatible major-version migration may remove old entrypoints; do not preserve every historical deprecated method when the target release does not promise that compatibility.

claims.rule: Replace wall-clock-sensitive middleware tests with version-appropriate virtual time, but assert domain state before and after the threshold; record completion timestamps only when the operation itself waits. Use monotonic time for intervals.
claims.applicability: CE3 TestControl in the 2022 throttle/timeout tests; CE2 Clock API differs. Generator resolution, positive periods and cancellation assertions remain separate proof obligations, not consequences of executeEmbed.
claims.counterexample: Virtual time does not validate a real socket, blocking executor or foreign clock. A test that merely sleeps then checks elapsed time cannot establish that a nonblocking token bucket changed state.

claims.rule: Inference: before claiming a stateful middleware refactor is hardened, inspect assertions and primitive wiring; independently test expiry boundaries, nonconsecutive nonce replay and cancellation signals rather than inferring those properties from effects, parameter names or test titles.
claims.applicability: Source-only inference tied to narrow historical CE2 nonce and CE3 timeout examples. The observed unused Blocker and discarded Boolean are limits to the historical exemplar, not verified present-day vulnerabilities or executed exploit reports.
claims.counterexample: A narrow allocation fix can intentionally leave a documented unrelated expiry follow-up. Report that coverage gap separately rather than claiming the patch introduced every pre-existing weakness.
